sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Butler County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Butler County deeds and mortgages are filed with the county recorder at 130 High Street, Hamilton, OH 45011. The office's fee schedule lists 513-887-3192 for the main line and recorder@bcohio.gov for email questions, and it gives a separate number, 513-887-3154, for transfer and conveyance questions.

The recorder's home page says documents recorded from 1987 to the present are searchable online. It also carries a statutory warning that anything filed with the recorder is generally a public record, which matters if a deed or mortgage you sign carries personal details. The schedule promises a 24 hour turnaround on documents, and it asks for a self addressed stamped return envelope with each submission.

Hamilton holds the courthouse and has the biggest population of any Butler County city, so a seller who lives in town can walk a deed over. Sellers in Middletown, Fairfield, Oxford, Monroe, Trenton or Sharonville file in the same Hamilton office, because Ohio keeps a single recorder for each county.

sections.h2: What does it cost to file a deed with the Butler County recorder?
sections.html:
The schedule effective January 1, 2025 prints $39.00 for a deed, mortgage, lease or similar document of up to two pages, and says that figure includes the $5.00 preservation surcharge. Each page after the first two is $8.00. The state sets the base of these charges in section 317.32 of the Revised Code, which splits the first two pages into a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fund fee and allows a surcharge of up to $5. Ask the office for the current sheet before you mail a check, since fee schedules get revised.

sections.h2: What does the auditor do before the recorder accepts a Butler County deed?
sections.html:
The deed stops at the county auditor first. Under section 319.202, the grantee files a statement of value, and the auditor stamps the deed with the conveyance fee and a note that the filing was made. The recorder's schedule says a conveyance or exemption form and the parcel identification numbers are required with every deed.

The fee itself comes from two layers of law, and the schedule folds them into one line:

  • Section 319.54(G)(3) sets the auditor's fee for receiving the statement at $1, or ten cents for each $100 or fraction of $100 of value, whichever is greater.
  • Section 322.02 lets a county commission add a real property transfer tax capped at thirty cents on each $100 of value, which the grantor pays to the auditor.
  • The Butler County Recorder's sheet prints $3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price and asks for a check payable to the Butler County Auditor, with 50 cents per parcel number added for deeds.

Call the number on the schedule if your deed covers several parcels, since the per parcel charge repeats for each number.

sections.h2: Which Butler County transfers skip the conveyance fee?
sections.html:
Section 319.54(G)(3) lists transfers where no auditor fee applies, and the grantee then writes the reason on the statement instead of paying. The exemptions a Butler County seller or heir meets most often include:

  • A gift in trust or outright between spouses, or between a parent and a child or the child's spouse.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one already executed and recorded.
  • A transfer made only to give or release security for a debt.
  • A transfer under a court order, to the extent it is not the result of a sale made under that order.
  • A transfer where no money or other valuable consideration is paid and the deal is not a gift.
  • A transfer to a buyer who is not a dealer, solely as a step in a prompt resale to others.

The statute carries more exceptions than these, including government transfers and deeds for $100 or less. Because an exempt deed still needs the exemption form, ask the auditor which form fits before the closing agent files.

sections.h2: What gets a Butler County document rejected or surcharged?
sections.html:
The recorder's standardization page applies the rules of section 317.114 to documents prepared after June 30, 2009, and charges $20.00 more when a paper misses them. Court documents, plats, DD214s and state or federal documents are not covered. The page lists these requirements:

  • Type of at least 10 point, on paper no smaller than 8.5 by 11 and no larger than 8.5 by 14.
  • Black or blue ink only, with no highlighting.
  • One inch margins on both sides and the bottom of each page.
  • A three inch top margin on page one, kept clear for the recorder, auditor and engineer.
  • A one and a half inch top margin on every later page.

The fee schedule adds other points. A legal description must accompany every document, an affidavit must name the current owner, and a document notarized in Ohio needs a prepared by statement. Blanket assignments and blanket satisfactions are not accepted, so a payoff for several loans needs a separate release for each.

sections.h2: Can you record a Butler County deed electronically or watch for fraud?
sections.html:
The recorder accepts electronic filings through three services named on its eRecording page: Simplifile, CSC and the eRecording Partners Network. Title companies and closing agents usually file this way, which skips the mail and the return envelope. The office also runs a free Property Alert service. After you register with an email address and password, the system emails you when a document is filed under your name or legal description, so a forged deed would not sit unnoticed.

The recorder's home page links to a notice of increased recording fees effective January 1, 2025, and to an earlier notice that raised the reference fee in 2022. Both are good reasons to work from the office's current sheet rather than from an old deed packet.

sections.h2: What is Butler County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Butler County sits in southwestern Ohio along the Great Miami River valley, covers about 470 square miles, and borders Hamilton County to the south. It was formed in 1803 and is home to Miami University; Oxford is one of its seven cities. The Census Bureau counted 390,357 people in April 2020 and estimated 400,128 for July 2025, which is 2.5 percent above the 2020 base.

  • Share of homes lived in by their owners, 2020 to 2024: 69.9 percent.
  • Typical home value, owner-occupied units, 2020 to 2024 median: $258,500.
  • Median household income, 2020 to 2024: $81,590.
  • Housing units in July 2025: 158,143.

The figures come from Census QuickFacts. Interstate 75 and US 42, 27 and 127 run through the county, and the county is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area.

sections.h2: How should a Butler County owner plan a fast as-is sale?
sections.html:
A sale to a cash buyer follows the same road as any other: a deed, a statement at the auditor, and filing at the High Street counter. The title company or closing attorney normally carries the papers between the two offices. If you handle the deed yourself, call the auditor about the conveyance fee and the recorder about page count and the non-standard fee before you sign.

Inherited houses add steps. The person who signs must hold authority over the estate, so heirs should confirm with the probate court which paperwork the title agent will want attached. Sellers with a mortgage should expect the lender to file a release, and the $4.00 reference fee on the sheet applies to that kind of filing.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Butler County recorder?
faqs.a: The recorder's fee schedule lists 513-887-3192 and the email recorder@bcohio.gov. For transfer and conveyance questions, the same sheet gives 513-887-3154. The office is at 130 High Street in Hamilton.

faqs.q: How much is the first page of a deed in Butler County?
faqs.a: The first two pages together are $39.00 on the schedule effective January 1, 2025, and that figure includes the $5.00 preservation surcharge. Pages after the second are $8.00 each. Confirm the amount with the office before filing.

faqs.q: Who gets the conveyance fee check in Butler County?
faqs.a: The Butler County Auditor. The recorder's schedule says to make the transfer fee check payable to the auditor and prints the rate as $3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price, plus 50 cents for each parcel number on a deed.

faqs.q: Does Butler County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder's eRecording page names Simplifile, CSC and the eRecording Partners Network as the services it accepts. Most title companies already file through one of them.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded without a legal description?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule states that a legal description is required with every document submitted for recording, and Butler County deeds also need parcel identification numbers. A deed missing either will come back unrecorded.
